report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/eval/mint.py chunk 1 of 3: docstring claims about independence, scope, hygiene, git failure handling, and worktree detection checked against the visible code.
risks: mint.py:1-100 | high | Docstring claims about _mint_from_diffs (scope, cross-file, hygiene, secret-floor) cannot be verified in this chunk; if implementation differs, the independence guarantee is broken | Read chunk 2/3 and verify _mint_from_diffs against each claimed filter

mint.py:158-190 | medium | _JUNK_KEYWORDS list is case-sensitive and narrow; docstring claims it is deliberately narrow, but any future edit adding a lowercase keyword could silently reject real identifiers | Compare keyword set against all supported languages' reserved words

mint.py:190-210 | medium | _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES only groups c/cpp and js/ts; docstring says families group languages the import graph crosses, but the list is hardcoded and may miss other crosses | Verify imports.py for all language pairs that resolve across specs

mint.py:216-226 | low | _is_junk_label matches name shape first; a name like 'if' passes the regex and then hits the keyword set. The regex uses [^\W\d] which allows unicode letters but also some symbols (e.g., underscore) — verify it doesn't accept punctuation | Inspect regex behavior with edge cases

mint.py:228-232 | low | MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD hardcoded to 3; docstring rationale assumes three independent mints, but nothing here enforces independence of confirmations | Verify confirm_task implementation in later chunk

mint.py:250-260 | medium | DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH uses os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) — if the module is moved or installed as a zip, path may be non-writable; docstring claims sibling of harness.py's DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH but that is unverified | Compare with harness.py constant

mint.py:266-283 | high | _git returns None on any failure, but the return type is str | None; a caller that expects a string could crash. The docstring says 'never raise' but a None return is not a raise; verify all callers handle None | Read chunk 2/3 for callers

mint.py:285-320 | high | _is_linked_worktree reads .git file and checks 'gitdir:' prefix; the docstring claims structural inspection of the admin directory, but the visible code only reads the pointer and returns False if not a file — the structural check is not in this chunk | Read chunk 2/3 for the structural inspection

mint.py:285-320 | medium | _is_linked_worktree fails toward 'not ephemeral' (returns False) when pointer is unreadable; docstring says that is correct, but if .git is a symlink or permissions issue, it will mint from a worktree | Verify with a linked worktree with unreadable .git
todos: Read chunk 2/3 to verify _mint_from_diffs implementation against the docstring claims
Read chunk 3/3 for remaining functions and the mint store persistence logic
Inspect imports.py to confirm the language family grouping matches the import graph crossing claim

handoff.purpose: Review module docstring and initial constants/helpers: junk filter, language families, git wrapper, linked-worktree detection.

symbols.name: _IDENTIFIER_RE
symbols.note: Compiled regex for plausible identifier shape: optional leading $ or non-digit, then word characters.

symbols.name: _JUNK_KEYWORDS
symbols.note: Frozenset of reserved words and markers considered junk labels; case-sensitive.

symbols.name: _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES
symbols.note: Dict mapping LanguageSpec names to family keys; only c/cpp and js/ts grouped.

symbols.name: _language_family
symbols.note: Returns family key for a language name; None stays None.

symbols.name: _is_junk_label
symbols.note: Returns True if name fails identifier regex or is in _JUNK_KEYWORDS.

symbols.name: MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD
symbols.note: Integer threshold for confirmations before a minted task leaves quarantine.

symbols.name: _GIT_TIMEOUT
symbols.note: Timeout in seconds for git subprocess.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH
symbols.note: Path to the persisted mint store JSON file.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs git in repo_root, returns stdout on success or None on any failure.

symbols.name: _is_linked_worktree
symbols.note: Returns True if repo_root is a git linked worktree by inspecting .git file pointer.

claims.text: Every task in daedalus.eval.tasks today was hand-picked by a human who then verified the pick by running semantic_slice -- circular, because the label is graded against the exact process that produced it (see tasks.py:1-8).
claims.why: The claim about tasks.py is outside this chunk; no content of tasks.py is visible.

claims.text: This module mints must_include labels from a source that has no opinion about the import graph at all: a byte-for-byte diff of what actually changed on disk, either a landed offload edit or a real git commit.
claims.why: The minting logic is in _mint_from_diffs, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: DO NOT expand a minted must_include through graph.callees / the import closure -- here or anywhere downstream of this module.
claims.why: No code in this chunk expands anything; the prohibition is a directive, not a code behavior to verify.

claims.text: must_include is ONLY: symbols whose extracted source differs between before and after, plus symbols that were added or removed outright.
claims.why: The definition of must_include is implemented in _mint_from_diffs, not visible here.

claims.text: Minted tasks land with "tier": "quarantine" and "label_provenance": "independent_diff" and are barred from any go/no-go recall number until confirm_task has been called on them MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD times.
claims.why: The task construction and confirm_task logic are not in this chunk; only the threshold constant is defined here.

claims.text: SCOPE: a changed file is eligible as target OR as a label source only if it appears in cached_index(repo)["modules"] -- the exact membership test slice.py's own neighborhood expansion uses (rel in modules, slice.py around line 225; that is THE scope boundary, not a second opinion about it).
claims.why: The scope check is inside _mint_from_diffs, not in this chunk; the reference to slice.py is external.

claims.text: Changed files that fail this test are recorded in skipped_out_of_scope on the diagnostics returned alongside the task (and on the task itself when one is minted) -- never silently dropped.
claims.why: Recording behavior is in _mint_from_diffs, not visible here.

claims.text: CROSS-FILE ONLY: must_include never contains a symbol defined in the file chosen as target.
claims.why: Enforced in _mint_from_diffs, not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A commit/edit where only one in-scope file has any diffed symbols therefore has no valid label source at all: it mints nothing rather than minting a label=[] task.
claims.why: This behavior is in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: THE SAME GUARD APPLIES AFTER LABEL HYGIENE BELOW: the junk / cross-language / secret-floor filters can themselves drain every candidate label, and an emptied-by-filtering must_include is exactly as vacuous as an empty one from a single-file diff -- _mint_from_diffs re-checks non-emptiness once, after filtering, and mints nothing (with a reason) if nothing survives.
claims.why: The re-check is inside _mint_from_diffs, not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: JUNK: a diffed name that fails _is_junk_label ... never becomes a must_include entry -- dropped names land in labels_filtered_junk (sorted).
claims.why: The application of _is_junk_label is in _mint_from_diffs; the recording of filtered names is also there.

claims.text: This list is deliberately narrow: a name that is a real, commonly-used identifier in even one supported language (delete as a Python/Django method, New as a Go exported constructor) is NOT junk just because it is also a reserved word in some other language.
claims.why: The _JUNK_KEYWORDS set (lines 158-190) does not include 'delete', 'new', 'default', 'case', 'switch', 'static', 'of', 'in', and the matching is case-sensitive, so 'New' would not match 'new'.

claims.text: CROSS-LANGUAGE: a label may only come from a file whose language FAMILY (_language_family(languages.spec_for(...).name)) matches the TARGET's ... Filtered names land in labels_filtered_cross_language (sorted).
claims.why: _language_family is defined here and works as described, but the filtering and recording are in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: Families group languages the slicer's own import graph routinely crosses (a C++ file and its own .h; a .ts file and the .js it imports) -- those are NOT cross-language for this filter's purposes.
claims.why: The claim about import graph crossing is external; _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES does group c/cpp and js/ts, but whether the import graph crosses those is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule is run against every anchor CANDIDATE's current content before target selection.
claims.why: The call to secret_floor_rule is in _mint_from_diffs, not visible here.

claims.text: A file that trips the floor is dropped from the ANCHOR POOL (recorded in skipped_secret_floor) ... AND from label consideration ... Filtered names land in labels_filtered_secret_floor (sorted).
claims.why: The recording and filtering are in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: Every LanguageSpec name NOT listed here maps to its own singleton family (its prior, unchanged behavior) -- this is purely additive grouping, not a relaxation of the filter for any language pair not named below.
claims.why: _language_family returns the input name unchanged for any key not in _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES, so each unlisted language maps to itself.

claims.text: None (no LanguageSpec) stays None and therefore never equals any real family, same fail-closed behavior as before this grouping existed.
claims.why: If lang_name is None, the function returns None immediately; None is not a key in _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES, so it never equals any family.

claims.text: Checked name-shape-first (a non-identifier like <anonymous> never reaches the keyword set at all).
claims.why: The function first calls _IDENTIFIER_RE.match(name) and returns True immediately if no match, so '<anonymous>' (which fails the regex) returns True before the keyword check.

claims.text: The keyword check is intentionally case-SENSITIVE ... name is matched as-is, never lowercased.
claims.why: The code does `return name in _JUNK_KEYWORDS` with no lowercasing; the set contains lowercase words, so 'New' would not match 'new'.

claims.text: Name-shape check: unicode-aware ... and allows a leading/embedded $ ... on top of the universal letter/digit/underscore identifier shape.
claims.why: The regex r"^(?:[^\W\d]|\$)[\w$]*$" uses \w which is unicode-aware in Python 3, allows a leading $ or any non-digit non-underscore word character, and allows $ anywhere after the first character.

claims.text: The set below is further limited to words that are reserved in EVERY supported language and implausible as a real symbol name in any of them -- unlike new/delete/default/case/switch/static/of/in, which are ordinary, common identifiers in at least one supported language.
claims.why: The set omits those words, and the comment explicitly explains why. The set includes words like 'if', 'else', etc., which are indeed keywords across many languages.

claims.text: Run git in repo_root; stdout on success, None on ANY failure (missing git, not a repo, bad ref, timeout, non-zero exit). Minting must degrade to "nothing minted", never raise.
claims.why: The try/except catches OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError (which includes TimeoutExpired), and returns None if returncode != 0. It never raises from the subprocess call. However, if repo_root is not a string, Path operations could raise, but that is not the documented failure mode.

claims.text: Minting must degrade to "nothing minted", never raise -- a caller looping over commits or landed edits cannot be allowed to die on the first unreadable one.
claims.why: The function returns None on any caught failure, so a caller that handles None will not crash. The function itself does not raise for the documented failure modes.

claims.text: A linked worktree is by construction temporary: daedalus.spine.attempt creates one per candidate and deletes it in a finally:.
claims.why: The behavior of daedalus.spine.attempt is external to this chunk.

claims.text: Minting from one therefore writes a task that can NEVER be evaluated again -- daedalus.eval.tasks.resolve_task_repo takes the absolute-path branch, finds the directory gone, and raises cannot resolve task repo label for the rest of that task's life.
claims.why: The behavior of resolve_task_repo is external.

claims.text: Detection is the git on-disk contract, not a path heuristic: git worktree add writes .git as a FILE holding a gitdir: pointer, whereas a primary checkout has .git as a DIRECTORY.
claims.why: The code checks if .git is a file and then reads it and checks for 'gitdir:' prefix. It does not use path heuristics like 'worktrees' in the path.

claims.text: A bare repo and a plain non-repo directory both read as "not a linked worktree" and are left to the existing git-failure paths, which already degrade to "nothing minted".
claims.why: If .git is not a file, the function returns False immediately, which is consistent with the claim.

claims.text: The pointer alone is NOT enough ... a SUBMODULE also has .git as a gitdir: file, and a submodule checkout is perfectly permanent -- refusing to mint from one would be a false refusal.
claims.why: The visible code only checks the pointer and returns False if not a file. The structural inspection that distinguishes submodules from linked worktrees is not in this chunk (it likely appears in chunk 2).

claims.text: Nor is the pointer's PATH enough: matching a worktrees path component would fire on any ordinary repository that happens to live under a directory someone named worktrees.
claims.why: The code does not inspect the pointer's path in this chunk, but the claim is about the design rationale; the actual structural inspection is in later lines.

claims.text: So the admin directory the pointer resolves to is inspected STRUCTURALLY, which is what actually distinguishes them ... commondir and gitdir together appear only in the linked-worktree admin layout.
claims.why: The structural inspection is not in this chunk; the code shown only reads the pointer and returns False if not a file. The rest is presumably in chunk 2.

claims.text: Requiring BOTH means an unreadable or unexpected target fails toward "not ephemeral", i.e. toward minting -- which is the correct direction for a false negative here.
claims.why: The failure direction depends on the full implementation, not visible here.

observations.what: _is_linked_worktree currently only reads the .git file and checks for 'gitdir:' prefix; the structural inspection described in the docstring is not present in this chunk.

_git returns None on failure, but the return type is str | None; callers must handle None. The docstring says 'never raise', but the function could raise TypeError if repo_root is not a string (e.g., a Path object) because subprocess.run expects a string or path-like; Path is acceptable, but a non-path object could raise.

_JUNK_KEYWORDS includes 'this' and 'self' as junk, but the docstring says these are never legitimate exported symbol names; however, 'self' is a common parameter name in Python and could appear as a method name? Actually 'self' is not a valid method name in Python, but 'this' could be a valid identifier in some languages (e.g., JavaScript object property). The docstring claims the set is narrow, but 'this' is a common property name in JS. This could be a false positive.

The regex _IDENTIFIER_RE allows leading '$' and then [\w$]*, but \w in Python includes underscore and alphanumerics; it does not include '$' except as an explicit alternative. This matches the docstring. However, it also allows a leading underscore, which is fine. It does not allow a leading digit, which is correct.

DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH is computed using os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), which assumes the module file is on a filesystem and writable. If the package is installed in a read-only location, writing to this path will fail. The docstring says it is a sibling of harness.py's DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH, but that is unverified.
